title.de: Der Komparativ: bigger than, more useful
title.it: Il comparativo: bigger than, more useful

goal.sl: Primerjaš dve stvari s -er in more + than, pišeš bigger, nicer in happier, rečeš better, worse in further ter koliko: much, a lot, a bit.
goal.de: Du vergleichst zwei Dinge mit -er und more + than, schreibst bigger, nicer und happier, sagst better, worse und further und wie viel: much, a lot, a bit.
goal.it: Confronti due cose con -er e more + than, scrivi bigger, nicer e happier, dici better, worse e further e di quanto: much, a lot, a bit.
goal.en: You can compare two things with -er and more + than, spell bigger, nicer and happier, say better, worse and further, and how much: much, a lot, a bit.

say.sl: Kratke besede dobijo **-er** in **than** (kot, od), ko primerjaš dve stvari: **old, older** (star, starejši); **tall, taller** (visok, višji). **Old Wilf is older than Jack.** (Stari Wilf je starejši od Jacka.) **Jack is taller than Harry.** (Jack je višji od Harryja.) Slovenski od je tu **than**, nikoli *from*.
say.de: Kurze Wörter bekommen **-er** und **than** (als), wenn du zwei vergleichst: **old, older** (alt, älter); **tall, taller** (groß, größer). **Old Wilf is older than Jack.** (Der alte Wilf ist älter als Jack.) **Jack is taller than Harry.** (Jack ist größer als Harry.) **than** heißt als, nie *as*.
say.it: Le parole brevi prendono **-er** e **than** (di, che) per confrontare due cose: **old, older** (vecchio, più vecchio); **tall, taller** (alto, più alto). **Old Wilf is older than Jack.** (Il vecchio Wilf è più vecchio di Jack.) **Jack is taller than Harry.** (Jack è più alto di Harry.) Di qui è **than**, mai *of*.
say.en: Short words take **-er** and **than** to compare two things: **old, older**; **tall, taller**. **Old Wilf is older than Jack.** **Jack is taller than Harry.** (never *Jack is taller as Harry.*)

say.sl: Pravopis: končni **-e** dobi samo **-r**: **nice, nicer** (prijeten, prijetnejši); **late, later** (pozen, poznejši). En samoglasnik + en soglasnik se podvoji: **big, bigger** (velik, večji); **hot, hotter** (vroč, bolj vroč); **wet, wetter** (moker, bolj moker). Soglasnik + **-y** postane **-ier**: **happy, happier** (srečen, srečnejši); **busy, busier**; **easy, easier** (lahek, lažji).
say.de: Die Schreibung: Ein **-e** am Ende bekommt nur **-r**: **nice, nicer** (nett, netter); **late, later** (spät, später). Ein Vokal + ein Konsonant wird verdoppelt: **big, bigger** (groß, größer); **hot, hotter** (heiß, heißer); **wet, wetter** (nass, nasser). Konsonant + **-y** wird zu **-ier**: **happy, happier** (froh, froher); **busy, busier**; **easy, easier** (leicht, leichter).
say.it: L'ortografia: una **-e** finale prende solo **-r**: **nice, nicer** (gentile, più gentile); **late, later** (tardi, più tardi). Una vocale + una consonante raddoppia: **big, bigger** (grande, più grande); **hot, hotter** (caldo, più caldo); **wet, wetter** (bagnato, più bagnato). Consonante + **-y** diventa **-ier**: **happy, happier** (felice, più felice); **busy, busier**; **easy, easier** (facile, più facile).
say.en: The spelling: a final **-e** takes only **-r**: **nice, nicer**; **late, later**. One vowel + one consonant doubles: **big, bigger** (never *biger*); **hot, hotter**; **wet, wetter**. A consonant + **-y** becomes **-ier**: **happy, happier** (never *happyer*); **busy, busier**; **easy, easier**.

say.sl: Dolge besede dobijo **more** (bolj): **useful, more useful** (koristen, bolj koristen); **famous, more famous** (slaven, bolj slaven); **expensive, more expensive** (drag, dražji). Nikoli obojega: **bigger**, nikoli *more bigger*. Dvozložne na **-y** ostanejo pri **-ier**: **happier**. Nekatere gredo na oba načina: **quieter** ali **more quiet** (bolj tih).
say.de: Lange Wörter bekommen **more** (mehr): **useful, more useful** (nützlich, nützlicher); **famous, more famous** (berühmt, berühmter); **expensive, more expensive** (teuer, teurer). Nie beides: **bigger**, nie *more bigger*. Zweisilbige auf **-y** bleiben bei **-ier**: **happier**. Manche gehen beides: **quieter** oder **more quiet** (ruhiger).
say.it: Le parole lunghe prendono **more** (più): **useful, more useful** (utile, più utile); **famous, more famous** (famoso, più famoso); **expensive, more expensive** (caro, più caro). Mai tutti e due: **bigger**, mai *more bigger*. Quelle di due sillabe in **-y** restano con **-ier**: **happier**. Alcune vanno in tutti e due i modi: **quieter** o **more quiet** (più tranquillo).
say.en: Long words take **more**: **useful, more useful**; **famous, more famous**; **expensive, more expensive**. Never both: **bigger** (never *more bigger*). Words of two syllables in **-y** keep **-ier**: **happier**. A few go either way: **quieter** or **more quiet**.

say.sl: Tri so posebne: **good, better** (dober, boljši); **bad, worse** (slab, slabši); **far, further** (daleč, dlje). **Arthur's honey is better than the shop's.** (Arthurjev med je boljši od trgovinskega.) **The weather is worse today.** (Danes je vreme slabše.) **farther** je tudi prav. Nikoli *gooder*, *badder*.
say.de: Drei sind eigen: **good, better** (gut, besser); **bad, worse** (schlecht, schlechter); **far, further** (weit, weiter). **Arthur's honey is better than the shop's.** (Arthurs Honig ist besser als der aus dem Laden.) **The weather is worse today.** (Heute ist das Wetter schlechter.) **farther** ist auch richtig. Nie *gooder*, *badder*.
say.it: Tre sono a parte: **good, better** (buono, migliore); **bad, worse** (cattivo, peggiore); **far, further** (lontano, più lontano). **Arthur's honey is better than the shop's.** (Il miele di Arthur è migliore di quello del negozio.) **The weather is worse today.** (Oggi il tempo è peggiore.) Anche **farther** è giusto. Mai *gooder*, *badder*.
say.en: Three stand alone: **good, better** (never *gooder*); **bad, worse** (never *badder*); **far, further**. **Arthur's honey is better than the shop's.** **The weather is worse today.** **farther** is right too.

say.sl: Za **than** pride samostalnik ali **me**, **him**, **us**: **Sam is taller than me.** (Sam je višji od mene.) Prav je tudi **than I am**. Koliko: **much bigger** (veliko večji), **a lot colder** (veliko bolj mrzlo), **a bit older** (malo starejši), nikoli *very bigger*. Vprašanje: **Which is older, the inn or the school?** (Kaj je starejše, gostilna ali šola?)
say.de: Nach **than** kommt ein Nomen oder **me**, **him**, **us**: **Sam is taller than me.** (Sam ist größer als ich.) **than I am** ist auch richtig. Wie viel: **much bigger** (viel größer), **a lot colder** (viel kälter), **a bit older** (ein bisschen älter), nie *very bigger*. Die Frage: **Which is older, the inn or the school?** (Was ist älter, das Gasthaus oder die Schule?)
say.it: Dopo **than** viene un nome o **me**, **him**, **us**: **Sam is taller than me.** (Sam è più alto di me.) Anche **than I am** è giusto. Di quanto: **much bigger** (molto più grande), **a lot colder** (molto più freddo), **a bit older** (un po' più vecchio), mai *very bigger*. La domanda: **Which is older, the inn or the school?** (Qual è più vecchia, la locanda o la scuola?)
say.en: After **than** comes a noun or **me**, **him**, **us**: **Sam is taller than me.** **than I am** is right too. To say how much: **much bigger** (never *very bigger*), **a lot colder**, **a bit older**. To ask: **Which is older, the inn or the school?**

exercises.text: Jack is ___ (young) ___ Sam, but he is ___ (tall). His farm is ___ (high) up on the fell, and it's ___ (cold) there than in the village. — Is the village ___ (nice)? — It's ___ (busy), and the ale at the inn is much ___ (good)!

translation.sl: Jack je mlajši od Sama, a višji. Njegova kmetija je višje na hribu in tam je bolj mrzlo kot v vasi. — Je vas lepša? — Bolj živahna je, pivo v gostilni pa je veliko boljše!
translation.de: Jack ist jünger als Sam, aber größer. Sein Hof liegt höher am Berg, und dort ist es kälter als im Dorf. — Ist das Dorf schöner? — Es ist belebter, und das Bier im Gasthaus ist viel besser!
translation.it: Jack è più giovane di Sam, ma più alto. La sua fattoria è più in alto sul monte, e lassù fa più freddo che in paese. — Il paese è più bello? — È più vivace, e la birra della locanda è molto migliore!
translation.en: Jack is younger than Sam, but he is taller. His farm is higher up on the fell, and it's colder there than in the village. — Is the village nicer? — It's busier, and the ale at the inn is much better!
